content: A related line of research has developed computational approaches to investigate language use and variation in discourse about complex sociopolitical issues in the media. For example, some work has drawn upon political communication theory to automatically detect the framing of an issue BIBREF41, BIBREF42, BIBREF43 through both supervised classification BIBREF44, BIBREF45 and unsupervised methods, such as topic modeling and lexicon induction BIBREF46, BIBREF47, BIBREF48. Scholars have also developed computational methods to identify lexical cues of partisan political speech, political slant in mass media, and polarization in social media BIBREF49, BIBREF50, BIBREF48.
